Computer Vision for Urban Waste and Infrastructure Monitoring in Malta

Project overview

Compare classical supervised detectors, prompt-based foundation models and representation-learning attribute classifiers for two municipal monitoring tasks: kerbside domestic-waste detection (MDWD) and traffic-sign condition assessment (MTSD).

MDWD

30225 images / 211512 boxes / 3598 unique sources (5 classes).

MTSD

7482 QA images / 20509 boxes in groups GRP-1, GRP-10, GRP-11, GRP-2, GRP-3, GRP-4, GRP-5, GRP-6, GRP-7, GRP-8, GRP-9.

Research questions and evidence matrix

RQ1 FINAL

How do modern supervised detector families and model scales (YOLO11/12/26, RF-DETR) compare on Maltese kerbside domestic-waste detection?

Experiments
MDWD YOLO11/12/26 n-l benchmark suites (Results/MDWD-Runs, Results/MDWD-Results)
RF-DETR nano run (excluded from headline tables until normalised)
Tables / figures
Documents/Final-Tables (mdwd_detection_results.csv)
Documents/Final-Figures/Robustness-Slices (per-class / slice figures)
Limitations
RF-DETR is a single nano-scale run without a normalised summary; the cross-family claim is YOLO-internal until that is fixed. Split leakage was measured and found negligible (max 0.48 pp).

RQ2 PILOT

Can zero-shot, prompt-based foundation models (SAM 3/3.1, Cosmos Reason2, LocateAnything) replace or complement supervised training for these municipal detection tasks?

Experiments
PromptDetect batch evaluations (Results/PromptDetect/BatchEvaluation)
Tables / figures
Documents/Final-Tables (promptdetect_results.csv)
PromptDetect run plots and GT-vs-prediction overlays
Limitations
Only pilot-scale MDWD runs exist (5-10 images, exploratory prompts); the fixed-protocol MDWD and MTSD evaluations are pending. Cosmos and LocateAnything emit no per-box confidence, so AP is not comparable across models - compare on precision/recall/F1/matched IoU.

RQ3 PENDING

Which adaptation strategy (frozen linear probe, LoRA, full fine-tuning) and model size over which pretrained backbone family (DINOv3, V-JEPA 2.1, ConvNeXt, LingBot-Vision) best supports multi-attribute traffic-sign condition assessment?

Experiments
16-variant size/adaptation matrix, completed 2026-07-13 on the eight-group snapshot (AttributeClassification/outputs/reports/size_ablation.{csv,md})
Historical six-variant round, GRP-1..GRP-3 snapshot (AttributeClassification/outputs, comparison.{csv,md})
Tables / figures
Documents/Final-Tables (mtsd_attribute_results.csv)
AttributeClassification/outputs/reports/size_ablation.csv
AttributeClassification/outputs/reports/comparison_macro_f1.png
Documents/Final-Figures/Robustness-Slices (per-head / condition figures)
Limitations
The 16-variant matrix is valid for the recorded eight-group manifest snapshot (GRP-1..GRP-3, GRP-5..GRP-9, 13,862 crops); GRP-10/11 Final-QA arrived after training, so a final-scope decision (freeze the snapshot vs re-run) is pending the annotation freeze. The historical six-variant round remains a GRP-1..GRP-3 snapshot. The condition head is the weakest (class imbalance).

RQ4 PENDING

What are the operational trade-offs - annotation effort, training cost, model size, latency, maintenance - between the supervised, prompt-based and attribute-classification paradigms?

Experiments
Annotation-effort report (Documents/Final-Reports/Annotation-Effort)
Inference-speed benchmark (pending)
Tables / figures
operational_comparison.csv (Annotation-Effort report)
Documents/Final-Tables (model_efficiency_results.csv - pending)
Documents/Final-Figures/Annotation-Effort
Limitations
Manual annotation-hour values are not recorded; the inference-speed benchmark has not been executed. Dimensions are reported raw - no composite ranking is computed.

RQ5 FINAL

How reliable are the collected datasets and reported results - annotation quality, integrity, split leakage and statistical uncertainty?

Experiments
Dataset integrity report (Documents/Final-Reports/dataset_integrity_report.md)
MDWD leakage sensitivity analysis (Documents/Final-Reports/MDWD-Leakage-Analysis)
MTSD annotation QA audits (Scripts/MTSD-Scripts/MTSD-AnnotationQA/outputs)
Bootstrap uncertainty (Documents/Final-Reports/Statistical-Uncertainty)
Tables / figures
leaked_source_identities.csv, bootstrap_results.csv
Documents/Final-Figures/Statistical-Uncertainty
Limitations
Bootstrap CIs currently cover stored MDWD detection predictions, the historical attribute snapshot (reconstructed from confusion matrices) and pilot PromptDetect runs; final-run uncertainty remains pending where the underlying experiments are pending.

Methodological notes

Percentile intervals; paired comparisons resample identical unit indices on both sides; no result is labelled "statistically significant" - the criterion reported is whether the CI excludes zero. Pilot-run intervals validate the pipeline only.

Failure cases (existing assets only)

Limitations and unresolved work

  • MTSD attribute results are a historical GRP-1..GRP-3 snapshot; the final-scope attribute round is pending and results must not be generalised to the expanded corpus.
  • MTSD supervised detection is pending (no training runs; Results/MTSD-* empty).
  • All existing PromptDetect evaluations are pilots (<100 images, exploratory prompts) - pipeline validation only, not dissertation evidence.
  • RF-DETR has a single nano-scale run whose metrics are not normalised into the consolidated tables; it is excluded from cross-family claims.
  • Cosmos Reason2 and LocateAnything emit no per-box confidence; their AP collapses to a single operating point and is not comparable to confidence-ranked AP (compare on precision/recall/F1/matched IoU).
  • Manual annotation-hour/cost values are not recorded; the effort report shows them as 'not recorded' rather than estimating them.
  • Low-support robustness slices are marked insufficient_support and must not be quoted as findings.
  • MDWD integrity findings {'out_of_range_box': 15, 'empty_annotation': 5, 'source_in_multiple_splits': 30} - split leakage was independently measured as negligible (max 0.48 pp); 15 out-of-range boxes and 5 empty annotations are train-split only.
